bookDetails.title: The Great Book of World Games
bookDetails.subtitle: 56 Games from 4,600 Years of Human Play — Rules, Boards and Stories from 39 Cultures, Ready to Play Tonight
bookDetails.author: Emre Doğan

description.text:
A reference book you play from.

The Great Book of World Games sets out 56 traditional games from 39 cultures, from the royal graves of Ur to a Zulu playground, and it sets them out so you can play them tonight. Each game gets two facing pages: the book lies open on the table and nobody has to turn a page in the middle of a turn.

WHAT IS INSIDE EACH ENTRY
· Players, time, age, materials and difficulty at a glance
· What to use instead of what — buttons, coins, dried beans, an egg box
· Numbered rules, one action to a line
· A board diagram drawn to scale
· The three questions every table argues about: what happens on a draw, what happens if nobody can move, and what happens when somebody plays an illegal move
· A shorter version to start with
· The work and the pages the rules were read from

SORTED BY HOW THEY WORK, NOT BY WHERE THEY ARE FROM
Most collections file games by country. This one files them by mechanism, in seven families — sowing, hunt and siege, race home, line and territory, the war board, chance and nerve, and games without a board. Put that way, the mancala games of Ghana, Sri Lanka and Buganda sit together and you can see what they share and where they part; the ancestors of chess sit together and you can watch six cultures solve the same problem six ways.

HONEST ABOUT WHAT IS KNOWN
Every rule set names its source. Where a historical record is incomplete, the entry says so and shows what has been reconstructed and on what basis. Where no source settles a question — most often the draw — the book makes a ruling and tells you it is the book's ruling, so you can overrule it. One page at the back is given to game origin stories that are widely repeated and are not true.

AT THE BACK
Full-size board templates you can photocopy. A materials guide. A glossary of the terms used for mechanics. Sources for every game. Three indexes — by culture, by number of players, and by time and age.

160 pages. Almost nothing in it has to be bought.
